disclaimer: First screen only — not legal approval. Houston and Los Angeles adopt the model codes with local amendments. Confirm with a licensed architect and the city before signing a lease.
ibc_note: IBC Table 1004.5 sets the occupant load a floor area is designed for. Houston enforces the 2021 Houston Construction Code and Los Angeles the Los Angeles Building Code (California Building Code); both carry Table 1004.5 with these factors. Values cross-checked against Washington's adoption of the same table (WAC 51-50-1004).

rules.title: Assembly, unconcentrated (tables and chairs)
rules.plain: 15 sq ft of dining floor for every seated guest.

rules.title: Exercise rooms
rules.plain: 50 sq ft of total floor for every person working out at one time.

rules.title: Business areas (outpatient clinics are Group B)
rules.plain: 150 sq ft of total floor for every person inside at one time, staff and patients together.

rules.title: Texas child-care licensing — indoor activity space
rules.plain: 30 sq ft of indoor activity space for every licensed child.

rules.title: Texas child-care licensing — outdoor activity space
rules.plain: 80 sq ft outdoors for every child using the play area at one time. Rotating groups lowers the area needed.

rules.title: California child-care licensing — indoor activity space
rules.plain: 35 sq ft of indoor activity space for every child, not counting bathrooms, halls, offices or the kitchen.

rules.title: California child-care licensing — outdoor activity space
rules.plain: 75 sq ft of outdoor activity space for every child in the licensed capacity.

rules.title: Day care (building-code occupant load)
rules.plain: The building code sizes exits at 35 sq ft per occupant. State licensing, above, sets how many children you may enrol.

cafe.why: Dining floor is about 65% of a food-service space; kitchen, counter, restrooms and corridors take the rest.

restaurant.why: Dining floor is about 60% of a full-service restaurant; a full kitchen takes more room than a café counter.

daycare.why: Activity rooms are about 60% of a child-care centre; bathrooms, halls, offices and the kitchen do not count.

gym.why: The exercise-room factor is already a gross figure.

clinic.why: The business-area factor is already a gross figure.

clinic_people_per_exam_room.why: One patient, one clinician and one person waiting or at the front desk per exam room.

recommended_headroom.why: Upper end of the recommended range is 1.5× the larger of the legal minimum and the market median.
